=== MULTI-SOURCE TOPIC CLUSTER: North Carolina sends vague letter to voters flagged by citizenship database ===

[Source 1 — www.democracydocket.com] (URL: https://www.democracydocket.com/news-alerts/north-carolina-sends-vague-letter-to-voters-flagged-by-citizenship-database/?utm_campaign=article-social&utm_content=1791925814&utm_medium=social&utm_source=bluesky):
Stated Claim / Post Context:
North Carolina sends vague letter to voters flagged by citizenship database

The letter provides flagged voters “with instructions on how to voluntarily request removal from the voter rolls if they were registered in error or provide information verifying their U.S. citizenship,” the board said in a press release Tuesday.

Actual Article Body:
By Jacob Knutson, Jen Rice

October 13, 2026

to see more of our voting rights news coverage when you search.

More than 1,000 North Carolina voters will begin receiving letters this week from the state election board requesting they verify their citizenship status — although the board claims compliance is voluntary.

The North Carolina State Board of Elections (NCSBE) is sending the vaguely worded letter to 1,392 registered voters identified as potential non-citizens through the federal Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlement (SAVE) database.

North Carolina voters have already begun sending in mail ballots for this year’s midterm election. Early in-person voting begins Thursday.

The letter provides flagged voters “with instructions on how to voluntarily request removal from the voter rolls if they were registered in error or provide information verifying their U.S. citizenship,” the board said in a press release Tuesday.

“Receiving a letter does not cancel an individual’s voter registration or automatically prevent an otherwise eligible voter from participating in the November 3 general election,” the board added. “Any voter challenge or determination of ineligibility must follow the procedures established under North Carolina and federal law.”

It was not immediately clear from the letter whether a voter who does not provide the requested information would be able to cast a ballot in the Nov. 3 midterm elections.

However, the letter states: “If you are a U.S. citizen and meet all other qualifications to vote, then you can remain registered and vote.”

The board asked the people flagged by SAVE to prove their citizenship even though North Carolina law has never required prospective voters to provide documentary proof of citizenship to register or remain registered.

The database initially flagged nearly 1,600 voters as potential non-citizens. But the board said Tuesday that around 200 of those voters were wrongly flagged and would not receive the letter.

Join 350,000 readers who rely on our daily and weekly newsletters for the latest in voting, elections and democracy.

Last April, Republicans on the NCSBE voted to feed the state’s registration data into SAVE over the objections of the board’s Democrats, who objected over privacy concerns and the risk of voters being disenfranchised through inaccuracies.

For years, the SAVE database existed as a tool for states to verify the immigration status of people applying for government benefits. The Trump administration, however, has overhauled the system into an expansive and flawed database to verify the citizenship status of people on state voter rolls.

The modified SAVE system routinely flags eligible voters as noncitizens, setting off increased state scrutiny on their voter registration, and therefore their ability to cast a ballot.

When Texas became the first state to use it last year, its Secretary of State’s Office said the system identified “2,724 potential noncitizens” on its voter registration list.

However, in subsequent investigations, county officials confirmed that at least 578 of those people were citizens, an error rate of at least 21%.

The Trump administration and Republican-led states attempted to justify the transformation of SAVE through unsubstantiated claims of widespread illegal voting by noncitizens. While such crimes do occur, countless reviews, studies and state audits have shown they are exceedingly rare and likely have not influenced the outcome of any election in modern history.

Letter: Ten ways in which Trump behaves like current and historical tyrants

Letter: Ten ways in which Trump behaves like current and historical tyrants

Actual Article Body:
President Donald Trump speaks with reporters before departing on Marine One from the South Lawn of the White House, Tuesday, Oct. 6, 2026, in Washington. (AP Photo/Alex Brandon)

Comment

Add as Preferred Source

Lately, I’ve seen a number of commentators and private citizens who want to dismiss arguments that Donald Trump is like Adolf Hitler or Hitleresque. In this crucial time when our very democracy and possibly the fate of the world is at stake, I feel obliged to respond and point out the many ways in which in fact Trump behaves like Hitler and other current and historical tyrants. Ten basic examples are below:

1. He has attempted to take over all aspects of the government, including the judiciary, and has done his best to silence any opposition by personal attacks, intimidation, and threats of incarceration.

2. He has done his best (and will continue) to suppress the media and curtail freedom of speech in academia and within the press, and, if necessary, declare a national emergency or use the Insurrection Act in order to forcefully stifle dissent.

3. By abruptly canceling foreign aid, he has cost the lives of millions of people, and many more will die due to his cuts to Medicaid and Medicare, all of which amounts to genocide, albeit by the pen.

4. Like other despotic leaders such as Hitler, Stalin, Putin, and many others, he is a megalomaniac who lacks vision and a moral compass and any compassion or regard for other people.

5. In attempting to interfere with and control the midterm and future elections, he clearly has no regard for democracy, freedom and constitutional law.

6. In that he is surrounded by oligarchs and captains of industry who are invested in power, his main goal, like other authoritarians, is to keep and maintain his own power, no matter what the consequences are or who is hurt.

This site is protected by reCAPTCHA and the Google Privacy Policy and Terms of Service apply.

7. Like other tyrants, he is bent on self-aggrandizement at the expense of human well-being and the entire planet.

8. Like Hitler, he lies and bases policy on perpetuating the big lies and promotes his tyranny by proclaiming that his rule is divinely inspired and by aligning himself with far-right groups.

9. Like Hitler, aided by rich industrialists and oligarchs, in his pursuit of power he seeks to conquer and acquire other sovereign territories, in this case Canada and Greenland.

10. Like Hitler, he sees himself as above the law and normal morality while he ruthlessly attacks minorities and disabled groups and, in the name of immigration reform, puts men, women and children in detention camps where many die due to unsafe and unsanitary conditions.

Frank J. Page, Salt Lake City
